strings.name: Limor Fried
strings.summary: Limor Fried shares electronic designs as Ladyada and founded Adafruit, combining hardware kits, manufacturing, educational resources and maker exchange. She promotes open designs and hands-on learning and helps build the open-hardware community. Employees and community contributors also create the company’s products, software and tutorials; these are not all solo works.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Birth date remains unconfirmed. Founding and New York operations, award years and report dates, and personal activities and team projects are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Founded Adafruit and promoted open-source hardware, advancing electronics education, maker culture and personal fabrication.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: MIT bachelor’s in electrical engineering and computer science (2003) and Master of Engineering (2005).
strings.facts.f2.label: Research residency
strings.facts.f2.value: Eyebeam research resident in 2005–2006, exploring hardware and developing the early business.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Open design and manufacturing
strings.highlights.h1.text: Through Adafruit, combines learnable, modifiable electronic designs with physical product sales to support personal making.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Sharing engineering practice
strings.highlights.h2.text: Uses tutorials and engineering programs to support hands-on learning and gives makers opportunities to show their work.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Adafruit collaborates with Mozilla
strings.timeline.t1.text: Mozilla announces joint testing of desktop Firefox Web Serial hardware workflows; this is a team project, not solely her implementation.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Ladyada engineering update released
strings.timeline.t2.text: The episode discusses boards, driver libraries and prototypes, distinguishing shipped work from ongoing development; this is the release date.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Wins Women in Open Source community award
strings.timeline.t3.text: Red Hat announces her community-category award, recognizing technical sharing and education.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Entrepreneur of the Year profile published
strings.timeline.t4.text: Entrepreneur profiles her as its 2012 winner; later 2013 reporting does not change the award year.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Appears on WIRED cover
strings.timeline.t5.text: Featured in the April 2011 issue discussing electronics making and open hardware.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Speaks at first Open Hardware Summit
strings.timeline.t6.text: Participates in the summit organized by Alicia Gibb and Ayah Bdeir; open hardware is a collective movement.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Announced as EFF Pioneer Award recipient
strings.timeline.t7.text: EFF recognizes her help in learning and adapting electronics; this is the announcement month, not confirmation of ceremony attendance.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Founds Adafruit
strings.timeline.t8.text: Begins with sharing electronic designs and selling kits; founding is distinguished from later New York operations.
